findings.title: Checkout trusts client-supplied price and tenant metadata
findings.description: The checkout route sends body.price_id and body.tenant_id directly to Stripe. A user can choose a cheaper price or another tenant's ID instead of the server mapping an allowed plan for the authenticated tenant.

exploitability.assessment: A logged-in user can tamper with billing state and paid access.

remediation.summary: Map plan IDs to server-owned Stripe price IDs, derive tenant_id from the authenticated user, and reject client-supplied billing ownership metadata.

findings.title: Webhook does not verify Stripe signature
findings.description: The webhook parses request JSON directly and trusts event metadata before upgrading tenant plan state. There is no stripe.Webhook.construct_event call or signature secret verification.

exploitability.assessment: Anyone who can reach the webhook can forge a checkout.session.completed event.

remediation.summary: Verify the Stripe-Signature header with the webhook signing secret, enforce idempotency, and map provider customer/session IDs to tenants server-side.
